The topic of thesis was to study the strategic management practices of the company with a strong growth history behind it. Find out whether they met the company's current size and future business requirements at the steering group level. The restaurant industry is highly competitive where changes in the operating environment occur rapidly. In this case, changes must be responded quickly but in a controlled manner. 
 
The aim of the study was to identify the strategic management practices that will be needed in the future for the company to succeed and become a significant player in its field. Qualitative research was chosen as the research method because in-depth information on the phenomenon under study was needed in order to be able to develop management methods. The research methods used were semi-structured and theme interviews, observation and netnography in order to achieve the research goal. The theory section explored new current management perspectives, which are living strategy, emotional intelligence and leading new era organization. 
 
The research was carried out as part of the management consulting work by conducting steering group interviews and observations, participating in management meetings, getting acquainted with the company's operating methods and available material in internet. The results of the study showed that the strategic management methods had not developed due to the company's strong growth to meet the company’s new changed business situation and future requirements. 
	 
Conclusions of the study were that current steering group work focuses too much on solving detailed day-to-day lower level operational issues without common holistic view of the most important strategic business activities. Correcting this requires prompt consideration of the management roles, tasks, required areas of expertise and composition of the management team.

Carolina Digital Repository (University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill)

This dissertation evaluates the effectiveness of the EU in promoting lasting liberalizing reforms in Central and Eastern Europe (CEE) before and after accession. It focuses on an area of governance with deep implications for both the quality of democracy and the prospect of economic development in the region - corruption control. The major finding is that since enlargement the EU has not had such strong direct and far-reaching effects as it did before accession. In analyzing corruption control both as a dependent variable as well as an independent one affecting FDI, I make three claims and substantiate each using a mixed-method approach featuring both time-series analyses and qualitative methods, such as case studies and expert survey data analyses. First, civil society development has stagnated since accession and so has its otherwise positive influence on corruption control: the exodus of most external donors and the EU's complicated procedures for applying for funding have crippled anti-corruption NGOs' capacities to monitor and advocate reforms. Second, EU leverage has been weaker after accession and anti-corruption reform has consequently slowed down: supranational pressures from the EU in the form of conditional funding and Cooperation and Verification Mechanism (in the cases of Bulgaria and Romania) as well as spillover effects from various chapters of the acquis have sufficed to prevent backsliding per se, but have not been able to reverse the post-accession trend of a slowdown in reform. Third, looking at corruption control as an independent variable, the effects of its stagnating trend post-accession include a decline in FDI. Encouraged by positive signaling from the EU confirming CEE countries' progression towards membership, FDI was steadily increasing during the pre-accession period and corruption control, improving or stagnant, was irrelevant for investors at that time. However, rates of investment have surprisingly dropped soon after accession, as investors have become less driven by cognitive shortcuts (the availability heuristic) causing them to assign disproportionate weight to information that is vivid or striking, such as the positive signals by the EU. In this new environment their concern about lack of progress in corruption control has led them to be more cautious.

sections.heading: From Butlins to Europe: Fodens Ladies in the 1960s and
paragraphs: ### From Butlins to Europe: Fodens Ladies in the 1960s and 1970s [[S4|Sport in History]] The Fodens Ladies, a pioneering team of women's football players, emerged from the shadows of the inter-war years in the 1960s and 1970s. Formed at a lorry manufacturing plant in Sandbach, Cheshire, the team contributed to a new vibrancy in the game, particularly during the period of women's football's marginalisation by the Football Association in the inter-war years. The team established itself as one of the pioneers of a female football revival and provided a public arena for several prominent international players of the period. [[S4|Sport in History]] The Fodens Ladies played charity matches and became a regular participant in the Butlin's Cup, winning it in 1969 and 1970.

They also undertook overseas tours, with team members receiving minimal support from the company. This paper draws on private personal archives, company records, holdings at the National Football Museum, national and local newspapers, and an in-house magazine, The Foden News, to situate the team within the context of Fodens Ltd and the wider context of women's football in the 1960s and 1970s. The paper concludes by signposting the next phase of research, which will explore in detail the biographies of key individuals involved in the Fodens team during this period. [[S4|Sport in History]] ### Biomechanical Contributions of the Trunk and Support Leg Hip in the Execution and Performance of Maximal and Submaximal Instep Kicks in Amateur Soccer Players [[S4|Sport in History]] This thesis investigates how the trunk and the hip of the supporting limb contribute to the execution and performance of maximal and submaximal instep kicks in amateur soccer players.

The biomechanics of the kick involves mechanical adjustments in the trunk and lower limbs that vary with the level of effort. This study focuses on kinematic and kinetic adjustments and energy transfer between body segments. The first study investigated the kinematic (KmS) and kinetic (KnS) strategies integrating the trunk and lower limbs to achieve maximal kicking performance. Fifty amateur soccer players were assessed.

[[S4|Sport in History]] Peak joint angles and moments of the trunk, the hip of the supporting limb, the hip and knee of the kicking limb, and foot and ball velocities were recorded. Canonical Correlation Analysis was used to assess the relationships between sets of variables.

sections.heading: THE EXCITEMENT OF FOOTBALL KICKS OFF IN QATAR: A SAMPLE
paragraphs: ### The Excitement of Football Kicks Off in Qatar: A Sample of Twitter Data Analysis [[S6|The Online Journal of Recreation and Sport]] The 2022 FIFA World Cup, hosted in Qatar, is set to bring unprecedented excitement and global attention. This article delves into the social reality of the World Cup through the lens of Twitter data analysis. The research, conducted by the Online Journal of Recreation and Sport, examines the opinions of Twitter users about the Qatar 2022 World Cup. [[S6|The Online Journal of Recreation and Sport]] The study involved analyzing 5,988 tweets posted by viewers under the theme "Qatar 2022 World Cup Overview." The analysis revealed four primary categories: "Organization," "Football Players," "Countries," and "Assessment." These categories were further divided into 36 codes and 11 sub-codes, providing a comprehensive understanding of the participants' perspectives.

[[S6|The Online Journal of Recreation and Sport]] In the sentiment analysis section, users expressed a wide range of emotions. Positive tweets accounted for 15,973, slightly positive for 30,533, negative for 3,228, slightly negative for 6,529, and neutral for 23,311. This data was further categorized into codes, categories, and themes using the "creative coding" option in the MAXQDA program. [[S6|The Online Journal of Recreation and Sport]] The research was structured in two main sections: content analysis of tweets and sentiment analysis of tweets.

The content analysis section focused on the organization, players, countries, and assessment of the World Cup, while the sentiment analysis section examined the emotional responses of the viewers. [[S6|The Online Journal of Recreation and Sport]] The completion of the codes created in the consensus took place over four months, ensuring a thorough and transparent process. The analysis was visualized using the "MAXMaps Hierarchical Code-Subcode Model" option, providing a clear and organized representation of the data. [[S6|The Online Journal of Recreation and Sport]] The findings of this study offer valuable insights into the social dynamics surrounding the World Cup, highlighting the diverse perspectives and emotions of the participants.

This research not only contributes to the understanding of the World Cup but also provides a glimpse into the broader social and political landscape of the 2022 World Cup. sections.heading: How Successful Are the Teams of the European Football Elite
paragraphs: ### How Successful Are the Teams of the European Football Elite off the Field? [[S1|Daily Yield prior News cycle]] In recent years, the European football elite has been increasingly focusing on corporate social responsibility (CSR) activities to enhance their sustainability efforts. This study examines the CSR activities of the Premier League and the Primera División teams in the 2018/2019 season. The findings reveal that while both leagues have made significant strides in CSR, the Primera División clubs have shown more comprehensive and detailed CSR practices.

[[S1|Daily Yield prior News cycle]] The study employs comparative analysis based on secondary databases, focusing on the teams' CSR aspirations and academic research results. Specific criteria were developed to evaluate environmentally and socially related CSR activities. Arsenal and Real Madrid were chosen as examples to showcase successful CSR practices that can serve as models for other sports teams. [[S1|Daily Yield prior News cycle]] At Premier League clubs, the practical application of CSR activities has been intensively developed.

Clubs share detailed statistical information about their actions, and some even publish their future plans. The quantity and detail of information found with Primera División clubs is varied. Some clubs provide extensive details about their CSR activities, while most clubs have superficial and lack exact descriptions of their CSR efforts. [[S1|Daily Yield prior News cycle]] The findings clearly indicate that the sports world is consciously shifting towards the realization of sustainable development, which requires a comprehensive reconnection of sporting society and an increase in awareness.

This shift is essential for the efficient and successful integration of CSR activities into sport. [[S1|Daily Yield prior News cycle]] ### What to Expect from Europe’s Most Valuable Company Before Tech Earnings [[S1|Daily Yield prior News cycle]] Before the companies' IPOs and deals, the daily yield of the tech sector is expected to be high. This is due to the high demand for tech stocks and the anticipation of significant earnings. The daily yield of tech stocks is expected to be around 10% in the coming weeks, making it a promising time for investors.

The daily yield is calculated based on the performance of the tech stocks in the previous week, and it is expected to increase as the earnings season approaches. [[S1|Daily Yield prior News cycle]] The daily yield is a measure of the expected return on investment in a particular stock or sector. It is calculated by dividing the expected gain by the initial investment amount.

sections.heading: The Global Economics of European Populism: Growth Regimes and Party
paragraphs: The article "The Global Economics of European Populism: Growth Regimes and Party System Change in Europe" delves into the dynamics of European populism, particularly focusing on the growth regimes theory. This theory posits that the core conflict driving populism is between debtors and creditors, which has been insightful but faces challenges in explaining why certain populist movements emerged before the global financial crisis and austerity measures. The article takes a different approach by examining shifts in political parties and party systems from the growth regime framework. It aims to explain the evolution of the cartel form of party that dominated European political systems from the late 1990s through the current period and why that form proved ineffective in responding to both the financial crisis and the political crisis that followed.

[[S2|Theseus (Ammattikorkeakoulujen)]] The article draws on the expanding literature on growth regimes to explain the rise of populist movements across the OECD. It argues that while the theory is insightful, it struggles to explain why populist movements predate the global financial crisis and austerity measures. The article proposes a different explanation by attributing the rise of populism to shifts in political parties and party systems, rather than the core conflict between debtors and creditors. [[S6|The Online Journal of Recreation and Sport]] The research was structured in two main sections: content analysis of tweets and sentiment analysis of tweets.
